Original contract C02/C07/C13 contemplates an independently admitted installed fresh stage; a conforming private copy is an eligible candidate for assessment. No specific copied instance/native policy is admitted.
Original helper direct gcc argv/Popen/current context and ordinary nonappend rawlog semantics are concrete preservation constraints.
Provider fresh preflight and child C05 inventory are separate checks; complete closure duty remains C05, not satisfied by the mechanical membership loop alone.

user_decisions: Assessing a conforming private copy does not itself change the original objective. Actual privileged copied-instance/native MAC policy adoption is a separate real decision and must be explicit; it is not inferred from Pro12 or this source comparison.
Using AppArmor, BPF supplement, or BPF-only changes the trusted mechanism/source/kernel-verifier/program-map/caller review scope. Each must preserve original C01–C15 and exact experiment behavior.

A hybrid of effective restrictions plus source/relevance/observer arguments can be evaluated under unchanged C05 if independently sufficient; granting arbitrary K inputs, dropping actual compiler inputs, adding flags/wrappers, replacing real proc census, increasing caps or weakening raw custody changes assurance/experiment and is not an authorized fix.
An enforcement-only preference can reject a hybrid proposal but does not turn finite source gaps into an impossibility theorem. Neither policy choice grants runtime/funding authority.
